title: Early-Cancellation Charge on Excess Flood Sale Cancellations
content:
**Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** sold shortly after the term start carry an early-cancellation charge.

**Rule.** The early-cancellation charge is 100 where the sale closing date is no more than 30 days after the term start, 50 where it is 31 to 90 days after, and nothing otherwise.

The sale closing date is the cancellation effective date of the Tidemark HomeFlood policy (HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies) whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record, cancelled for the sale. The days are counted from the term start on the excess policy record to the sale closing date. Amounts are in US dollars.

Each retention or charge set on a sale cancellation is subtracted from the returned premium — once that premium has been limited to the term premium less the minimum earned share, and before its single rounding to the cent — and the returned premium never falls below nothing.

| Sale closing date, days after the term start | Early-cancellation charge |
|---|---|
| no more than 30 | 100 |
| 31 to 90 | 50 |
| more than 90 | nothing |

**Boundaries.** A closing 30 days after the term start carries 100; 31 days, 50; 90 days, 50; 91 days, nothing. A returned premium of 40.00 against a charge of 50 becomes nothing, never a negative figure.
